messages.author: 5e649bb0b1e892e9
messages.subject: Missing method getChipType()
parts:
Dear Henrik

As you see, I can access almost all data from print(plm) with the
exception of "Chip type"
> print(plm)
RmaCnPlm:
Data set: TestSty250K
Chip type: Mapping250K_Sty
Input tags: ACC,-XY,QN
Output tags: ACC,-XY,QN,RMA,+300,A+B
Parameters: (probeModel: chr "pm"; shift: num 300; flavor: chr
"affyPLM"; treatNAsAs: chr "weights"; mergeStrands: logi TRUE;
combineAlleles: logi TRUE).
Path: plmData/TestSty250K,ACC,-XY,QN,RMA,+300,A+B/Mapping250K_Sty
RAM: 0.01MB
> getName(plm)
[1] "TestSty250K"
> getChipType(plm)
Error in UseMethod("getChipType") :
no applicable method for "getChipType"
> getTags(plm)
[1] "ACC" "-XY" "QN" "RMA" "+300" "A+B"
> getParameters(plm)
$probeModel
[1] "pm"

$shift
[1] 300

$flavor
[1] "affyPLM"

$treatNAsAs
[1] "weights"

$mergeStrands
[1] TRUE

$combineAlleles
[1] TRUE

> getPath(plm)
[1] "plmData/TestSty250K,ACC,-XY,QN,RMA,+300,A+B/Mapping250K_Sty"

It would be great if "getChipType(plm)" would return
"Mapping250K_Sty".

Best regards
Christian

parts: On Mon, Mar 10, 2008 at 5:41 AM, cstratowa <Christian...@vie.boehringer-ingelheim.com> wrote:

Dear Henrik

As you see, I can access almost all data from print(plm) with the
exception of "Chip type"
> print(plm)
RmaCnPlm:
Data set: TestSty250K
Chip type: Mapping250K_Sty
Input tags: ACC,-XY,QN
Output tags: ACC,-XY,QN,RMA,+300,A+B
Parameters: (probeModel: chr "pm"; shift: num 300; flavor: chr
"affyPLM"; treatNAsAs: chr "weights"; mergeStrands: logi TRUE;
combineAlleles: logi TRUE).
Path: plmData/TestSty250K,ACC,-XY,QN,RMA,+300,A+B/Mapping250K_Sty
RAM: 0.01MB
> getName(plm)
[1] "TestSty250K"
> getChipType(plm)
Error in UseMethod("getChipType") :
 no applicable method for "getChipType"
> getTags(plm)
[1] "ACC"  "-XY"  "QN"   "RMA"  "+300" "A+B"
> getParameters(plm)
$probeModel
[1] "pm"

$shift
[1] 300

$flavor
[1] "affyPLM"

$treatNAsAs
[1] "weights"

$mergeStrands
[1] TRUE

$combineAlleles
[1] TRUE

> getPath(plm)
[1] "plmData/TestSty250K,ACC,-XY,QN,RMA,+300,A+B/Mapping250K_Sty"

It would be great if "getChipType(plm)" would return
"Mapping250K_Sty".

On purpose, because should it return the chip type of the (input) data set or the (output) result set?  This makes a difference if you ask for the "fullname" chip type (e.g. including the "monocell" tag).  Instead do:

ds <- getDataSet(plm)
getChipType(ds)

and

ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm)
getChipType(ces)

and there is no double what you get.  The one you see in the output, is the chip type for the data set (the former).

/Henrik



Best regards
Christian

Thank you for your explanation. However, I do not understand it:

1, I get:
> getChipType(getDataSet(plm))

Error in UseMethod("getChipType") :
no applicable method for "getChipType"
> getChipType(getChipEffectSet(plm))

Error in UseMethod("getChipType") :
no applicable method for "getChipType"

2, In my personal opinion, getChipType() should return the chip type
listed with print(plm).
An alternative would be to list both input and output chip types and
use the methods
getInputChipType() and getOutputChipType().

Best regards
Christian
